title: Offload telemetry serialization to background workers and add request-level adaptive sampling
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Runtime p95 increases under bursty traffic due to synchronous span/metric/log serialization on hot request paths. The current OpenTelemetry exporter path performs JSON encoding and compression on the request goroutine, contributing to tail latency and GC pressure. Goal: Move serialization and network encoding off the hot path (background worker pool), implement request-level adaptive sampling to reduce payload volume for noisy endpoints, and provide a runtime flag to temporarily mute high-cardinality fields for emergency mitigation.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end request latency p95 for the inference runtime service improves by >= 8% in our internal synthetic burst test compared to baseline
Span/event serialization happens outside the hot request goroutine for >= 95% of requests in the load test (verified via trace tags)
Adaptive sampling reduces exported telemetry size by at least 25% for identified noisy endpoints without losing error traces
Runtime flag to mute high-cardinality labels can be toggled via console and applies within 30s without restart
No regressions in trace continuity — parent/child relationships preserved and trace IDs retained
technical_notes: Design: introduce a bounded background worker pool (configurable size) that accepts pre-serialized span payloads; workers will batch and send to exporters asynchronously.
We will keep trace context on the request path but offload format/encode/zip to workers. Use a small zero-copy buffer pool to reduce allocations.

Adaptive sampler: implement a lightweight per-endpoint reservoir sampler with exponential decay counters. Default sampler configuration will be conservative (favor capturing errors and small fraction of normal traffic).
Compatibility: maintain OTLP/gRPC exporter contracts. Worker errors should fallback to synchronous export for critical spans (configurable threshold).
Emergency mute: implement a feature flag in the config plane and a runtime toggle endpoint. When enabled, drop or truncate high-cardinality labels (user_id, session_id) and reduce histogram buckets.
Metrics: add counters for exported_bytes, worker_queue_depth, worker_drops, sampler_kept, sampler_dropped to monitor behavior.
Memory safety: use pooled byte slices (sync.Pool) and ensure workers respect context cancellation to avoid leaking goroutines.
Observability: add an internal trace span to measure serialization duration and worker queue time; surface in console dashboards.

2025-02-18 — Design review with infra and runtime teams. Decided to keep trace context synchronous, only offload CPU-heavy formatting. Agreed on bounded queue and backpressure policy (drop oldest when full). — Notes attached to design doc.

2025-03-03 — Integration tests added: queue full/backpressure behavior + verify sampler preserves error spans. Some flaky failures in CI due to race on pool release; fixed in PR #1089. — Luis

2025-03-05 — Canary rollout to staging in progress; monitoring worker_queue_depth and worker_drops. Initial telemetry shows worker_drops=0 and exported_bytes down 31% for inference-batch endpoint. — Luis
qa_notes: Run bursty synthetic load (stress-tool v2) with and without feature enabled. Validate p95 latency, worker queue depth, and that trace parent/child relationships remain intact. Test emergency mute toggle via console for 30s and verify labels truncated in exported traces. Verify no goroutine leaks after sustained 1h test.
release_notes: Improve runtime tail latency by offloading telemetry serialization to background workers and introduce adaptive sampling to reduce telemetry volume for noisy endpoints. Adds a runtime emergency mute toggle for high-cardinality fields.
